Logistics and transportation challenges: Transport logistics are complex for LPTs, which are oversized loads weighing more than 100 tons, but the challenges are particularly acute for LPTs used in hydropower. Many hydroelectric dams are sited in rugged or remote locations where access roads may feature weight-restricted bridges, steep grades, or tight curves. There is a limited domestic fleet of specialized vehicles that can transport LPTs, including multi-axle heavy haul trailers and Schnabel railcars (which suspend the transformer as part of the railcar frame), an example of which is shown in Figure 9. Facilities located along navigable waterways may be able to deliver LPTs by barge (Roberts 2021). Each transportation stage requires special permits for oversized loads from every jurisdiction along the route. Roughly 3% to 20% of a transformer’s total cost is related to shipping and logistics (U.S. Department of Energy 2024). Figure 9. LPT transportation via truck and type-240 Schnabel trailer. Safety and environmental regulation of transformers can pose delays for transformer replacements. U.S. Environmental Protection Agency regulations on mineral oil use add further compliance steps for asset owners, and the duration between removing an old transformer and installing a new one can be extended by these requirements. For example, switchyard renovations may have to contend with additional environmental permitting or permit amendments if the footprint or containment of a new transformer differs from the old one. Permitting delays coupled with other supply chain challenges such as long lead times further increase demand uncertainty for LPTs. Trade restrictions and import policies: International trade issues influence the LPT supply chain. In 2018, under section 232 of the U.S. Trade Expansion Act, the U.S imposed a 25% tariff on most imported steel. While the intent of the policy was to spur domestic steel production, instead transformer manufacturers faced higher material costs (Erickson 2022). An analysis from the American Public Power Association found that proposed duties on copper and other LPT inputs may affect transformer prices and could discourage energy projects that need step-up transformers (Ciampoli 2025). In discussion with stakeholders, original equipment manufacturers expressed concerns about sourcing from China, Russia, and other foreign entities of concern (FEOC) because of security and supply availability concerns. BABA and BAA policies: Two key policies govern domestic content requirements for both federal acquisition and the use of federal funds in infrastructure projects: the Buy American Act (BAA) and the Build America, Buy America Act (BABA).
